items.topic: Agent-manager base URL resolution for VerifyIdentity
items.context: VerifyIdentity needs to call POST /api/v1/identity/verify on agent-manager. The consumer (any scenario CLI) needs to know where agent-manager lives. Agent-manager already injects env vars into runs (VROOLI_AGENT_IDENTITY_TOKEN, VROOLI_SANDBOX_*), so injecting the API base URL follows the same pattern.

options.label: Dedicated env var VROOLI_AGENT_MANAGER_API_BASE
options.rationale: Agent-manager already injects env vars for runs. Adding one more is trivial and keeps the consumer zero-config. VerifyIdentity reads this env var internally. This is the simplest and most consistent approach — recommended.

options.label: Accept *HTTPClient parameter (caller configures base URL)
options.rationale: More flexible — caller controls the HTTP client and base URL. But this pushes configuration burden onto every consuming scenario, and they'd all end up reading the same env var anyway.

options.label: Both: env var with HTTPClient override
options.rationale: VerifyIdentity reads VROOLI_AGENT_MANAGER_API_BASE by default, but accepts an optional HTTPClient for callers who need custom configuration (e.g., tests, non-standard setups). More complex API surface but maximally flexible.

items.context: Related to D1 — the function signature determines how callers interact with verification. The sandbox pattern uses a free function (DetectSandbox) plus methods on the struct (IsSandboxActive). Identity could follow the same pattern with VerifyIdentity as a method on IdentityEnv.

options.label: Method on IdentityEnv: env.VerifyIdentity() (*VerifyResult, error)
options.rationale: Clean API — detect first, then verify. Token is encapsulated in the struct. No parameters needed if D1=A (env var provides base URL). Recommended for simplicity and consistency with sandbox pattern.

options.label: Method with client param: env.VerifyIdentity(client *HTTPClient) (*VerifyResult, error)
options.rationale: Follows the spec description exactly. Gives caller control over HTTP configuration (timeouts, TLS). More testable without env vars. But requires caller to construct an HTTPClient even for the common case.

options.label: Functional options: env.VerifyIdentity(opts ...VerifyOption) (*VerifyResult, error)
options.rationale: Go-idiomatic extensibility — WithHTTPClient, WithBaseURL, WithTimeout. Most flexible but heaviest API surface for a single HTTP call.

items.topic: IdentityEnv struct: token-only vs. full metadata
items.context: The spec lists IdentityEnv with many fields (Token, RunID, TaskID, ProfileKey, ScopePath, IssuedAt, ExpiresAt, Meta). However, the research established that tokens are opaque to consumers — all metadata comes from verification. Having pre-verification fields on IdentityEnv would be misleading since they can't be populated without verification.

options.label: Token-only IdentityEnv (just the raw token string)
options.rationale: Honest API — the only thing available pre-verification is the token string. All claims come from VerifyResult after calling the endpoint. Avoids misleading struct fields that are always empty. Recommended.

options.label: Full metadata struct matching the spec description
options.rationale: Matches the spec exactly (Token, RunID, TaskID, etc.). But since tokens are opaque, these fields would need separate env vars for each claim or would always be zero-value until verification. Adds complexity without value.

items.context: When agent-manager returns 401 (invalid/expired/revoked token), the current handler returns JSON with {valid: false, error: '...'}. The consumer needs to distinguish 'token is bad' from 'network is down'.

options.label: 401 returns *VerifyResult with Valid=false (not a Go error)
options.rationale: Clean separation: Go errors = transport failures, VerifyResult.Valid=false = auth failures. Callers use 'if err != nil' for network issues and 'if !result.Valid' for bad tokens. This matches how the agent-manager handler already structures responses. Recommended.

options.label: 401 returns a typed Go error (IdentityError with claims)
options.rationale: Everything is an error — callers use errors.As to distinguish types. Simpler 'if err != nil' check but loses the structured result for 401 cases.

items.text: The dependency (agent-manager-identity-tokens) is completed. The verification endpoint exists at POST /api/v1/identity/verify and returns {valid: bool, claims: {run_id, task_id, profile_key, scope_path, iat, exp, meta}, run_status: string, error: string}. Claims use uuid.UUID in agent-manager but cli-core will use strings to maintain zero external dependencies.
